title: Route authority
description: Deployment fences, admission, and trust.
text:
Route authority and admission 
 A selected route must know which deployment is allowed to serve it. Troolio represents this with a route key, positive epoch, and deployment fingerprint in  AtomicRouteFence . An authoritative store compares the fence under the same transaction or lock that commits events. Promotion increments the epoch, so an uncommitted request from an older deployment fails. On this page Trust boundaries Operational use Example: Represent the current route 
 Trust boundaries 
 
 TrustedAtomicCommandIngressAdapter  binds the caller's command to an authenticated route and canonical request identity. 
 IAtomicCommandCurrentPrincipal  supplies current principal evidence; copied message headers do not grant permission. 
 OrleansAtomicNoSubscriberRouteAuthority  and  OrleansAtomicSubscriberRouteAuthority  review actor classes, handlers, and subscriber registrations before a selected path is admitted. 
 IAtomicRouteClusterLeaseAuthority  and selected-route silo admission keep the serving cohort aligned with the deployment record. 
 
 A matching completed receipt can be replayed after promotion only after the current owner/deletion checks and exact request, batch, and route fence comparison. A stale uncommitted request cannot write. The host owns authentication, authorization, process identity, deployment review, and retirement sequencing. 
 Operational use 
 Treat route promotion as a controlled deployment operation. Record the reviewed inventory and fingerprint, admit the new cohort, fence the old epoch, and verify pending operations before retiring it. Provider-specific admission is described in  SQL Server  and  KurrentDB . 
 Example: Represent the current route 
 The fingerprint is a SHA-256 digest of the reviewed deployment. The host gets its current epoch from its route authority, then passes the fence into the selected commit request. 
 public static AtomicRouteFence Fence(long epoch, string deploymentHash) =>
    new("counter-route", epoch, deploymentHash);

title: Orchestration
description: Event-only planning and durable subscriber delivery.
text:
Orchestration 
 An orchestration turns an event into another domain action. The source actor decides what happened; the listener chooses the next actor to contact; that destination actor validates the next command against its own state. On this page Follow the business relationship Keep state restoration separate Ordinary and selected event-only work Claiming durable subscriber work Failure, cancellation, and outside systems 
 For example, a registration actor produces  RegistrationRequested . A listener asks the workshop roster actor to record that registration. The same event can also feed a projection, but the projection's job is to update a reader's view. 
 Follow the business relationship 
 Start with three questions: which event triggers the workflow, which actor owns the next decision, and which business key identifies that work? In the workshop example, the event carries both registration ID and workshop ID. Those values make the destination explicit and let retries be recognized. 
 [OrchestrationStreamSubscription(typeof(RegistrationActor))]
public sealed class WorkshopEnrolmentOrchestration : OrchestrationActor
{
    public Task On(EventEnvelope<RegistrationRequested> envelope) =>
        System.ActorOf<IWorkshopRosterActor>(envelope.Event.WorkshopId.ToString("D"))
            .Tell(new AddAttendee(envelope.Event.Headers, envelope.Event.WorkshopId,
                envelope.Event.RegistrationId, envelope.Event.AttendeeId));

    public Task On(EventEnvelope<RegistrationCancelled> envelope) =>
        System.ActorOf<IWorkshopRosterActor>(envelope.Event.WorkshopId.ToString("D"))
            .Tell(new RemoveAttendee(envelope.Event.Headers, envelope.Event.WorkshopId,
                envelope.Event.RegistrationId));
}
 
 The subscription selects events from  RegistrationActor . The typed  On  methods handle request and cancellation separately. Returning the  Tell  task makes command dispatch part of the listener's observable work. The headers are forwarded for the ordinary internal-command protocol;  metadata  explains how Troolio creates the next message and causation context. 
 Keep state restoration separate 
 The registration actor's  On  method applies an event to its own in-memory state. It must be safe to call while replaying history. Sending the roster command there would repeat the workflow whenever the actor activates. 
 The orchestration listener is a separate role and receives its configured event delivery. See  replay and live events  for the boundary. 
 Ordinary and selected event-only work 
 An ordinary listener can issue internal commands within Troolio's transaction context. Its attribute and method do not by themselves establish that a store commits every involved stream atomically. Choose the actual route and provider according to the operation's requirements. 
 A selected event-only route plans a reviewed, closed set of participant events. It needs bounded planning, current route authority, supported handler classes, and a capable store that persists the required events, handoffs, and completion receipt. External effects belong behind durable intents rather than inside that precommit planner. 
 IEventOnlyOrchestrationStateStore  retains the frozen operation state.  IEventOnlyOrchestrationDeliveryStore  makes expected subscriber work discoverable and claimable after restart.  DurableEventOnlySubscriberExecutor  validates registered plan handlers and their allowed emissions. 
 Claiming durable subscriber work 
 A delivery identity names an operation, source envelope, and expected subscriber. A claim gives a worker a bounded lease; the returned fencing token must guard state changes. 
 public static Task<EventOnlyOrchestrationDeliveryLease?> Claim(
    IEventOnlyOrchestrationDeliveryStore store, Guid operationId, Guid envelopeId) =>
    store.TryClaimAsync(new(operationId, envelopeId, "roster-planner"),
        "worker-1", TimeSpan.FromMinutes(1));
 
 Claiming does not mean completion. A worker must register child work and participants before completing its receipt, and an old worker must not mutate state after a trusted takeover. The host provides durable store implementations, route admission, worker scheduling, and recovery. 
 Failure, cancellation, and outside systems 
 A repeated roster add should not increment a count twice. A cancelled registration should not be resurrected by a late add. The target actor needs durable business identity and lifecycle rules as well as message tracing. 
 A provider call or human approval introduces a longer-lived workflow. Record pending work and attempts explicitly, use idempotent providers, and record a definitive outcome as another domain command. A detached in-memory task cannot preserve that work through process loss. 
 For the complete practical treatment, follow  orchestration workflows ,  correlation and causation , and  notifications and background work . For selected atomic work, read  selected command route ,  atomic commit , and  recovery .

title: External effects
description: Durable intents, idempotency, and reminders.
text:
External effects and reminders 
 An atomic event commit does not make a network call, email, or reminder update atomic with event storage. Troolio models such work as an  ExternalEffectIntent  tied to a committed operation, request identity, serialized batch hash, subscriber, provider, and payload hash. On this page Durable intent protocol Reminder adapter Example: Register an effect intent 
 Durable intent protocol 
 ExternalEffectDispatcher.RegisterAsync  records a frozen intent after the event receipt is available.  DispatchAsync  calls an  IIdempotentExternalEffectProvider  with a stable key and records a terminal receipt.  RecoverPendingAsync  pages pending intents after restart. A provider must deduplicate by key for the full effect lifetime and return a terminal result only when the outcome is definitive; uncertain failures throw for retry. 
 IAtomicEventEffectIntentStore  supports a stronger path where event commit and effect intent are part of the same transaction, with  AtomicEventEffectTransaction  validating the receipt. A host must choose storage, worker scheduling, provider credentials, retention, and monitoring. If an intent is recorded only after the event commit, the host must account for the gap between those steps. 
 Reminder adapter 
 ReminderEffectIntent  describes register/update or unregister operations.  ReminderDesiredStateEffectProvider  requires a host that can preserve desired state and definitive superseded outcomes. A reminder is an external effect, so replayed event handlers must not directly mutate it. 
 Example: Register an effect intent 
 After the event transaction has a complete receipt, register an intent for an idempotent provider. A worker dispatches and records its terminal outcome separately. 
 public static Task<ExternalEffectIntent> RegisterEffect(
    IExternalEffectIntentStore intents, IIdempotentExternalEffectProvider provider,
    AtomicEventTransactionReceipt receipt, byte[] payload) =>
    ExternalEffectDispatcher.RegisterAsync(intents, provider, receipt,
        "send-email", "notification-handler", payload);

title: Recovery
description: Retries and pending work across providers.
text:
Recovery and retries 
 A retry must preserve the original operation identity and exact serialized event batch. The atomic store returns its prior receipt only after matching request identity, participant bytes, route fence, current ownership, and deletion fences. Changing any of those inputs is a conflict, not a new attempt at the same operation. On this page Recovery surfaces Incident handling Example: Resume pending effects Repair application read models 
 Recovery surfaces 
 
 
 
 Pending work 
 Recovery contract 
 
 
 
 
 Selected command 
 Operation recovery checks current route admission and persisted completion evidence before resuming. 
 
 
 Event-only subscriber 
 Delivery state and claim leases identify work that can be retried after a worker exits. 
 
 
 External effect 
 IExternalEffectIntentStore.ListPendingAsync  and  ExternalEffectDispatcher.RecoverPendingAsync  resume work with the original idempotency key. 
 
 
 Projection 
 Provider queue or marker state retains a handoff until the consumer applies and acknowledges it. 
 
 
 
 Provider implementations add their own journals, route pins, and retention rules. SQL Server keeps transaction evidence in its database. KurrentDB-based routes may coordinate KurrentDB and SQL state through a broker journal; this is not a distributed transaction across both systems. 
 Incident handling 
 First establish the committed receipt or current stream head. Then inspect pending delivery, effect, and projection records. Preserve operation IDs, request identities, route epochs, and provider receipts while investigating. Do not delete evidence merely to unblock a retry. See  troubleshooting  and  deployment checklist . 
 Example: Resume pending effects 
 A recovery worker lists pending durable intents and dispatches them through providers keyed by provider ID. Each provider must honor the original idempotency key. 
 public static Task<IReadOnlyList<ExternalEffectTerminalReceipt>> RecoverEffects(
    IExternalEffectIntentStore intents,
    IReadOnlyDictionary<string, IIdempotentExternalEffectProvider> providers) =>
    ExternalEffectDispatcher.RecoverPendingAsync(intents, providers, 100);
 
 Repair application read models 
 Projection catch-up and rebuilds  separates delivery recovery, versioned rebuilds, and bounded data repair.  Idempotency and ordering  explains which source evidence each consumer retains.

title: Agents package
description: Agent definition and run actors.
text:
Agents package 
 Troolio.Agents  models agent definitions and runs as event-sourced actors. It provides framework contracts and actors; it does not choose a model provider, tool runtime, credential store, or execution policy for the host. On this page Definition actor Run actor Example: Create an agent and a run 
 Definition actor 
 IAgentActor  accepts  RegisterAgent ,  UpdateAgentDefinition ,  SetAgentEnabled , and run lifecycle registration commands. Its events include  AgentRegistered ,  AgentDefinitionUpdated ,  AgentEnabledChanged ,  AgentRunStarted , and  AgentRunCompleted .  GetAgentDefinition  and  GetAgentMetrics  query the projected actor state. The definition records the agent's identity and configuration; the host decides who may modify it. 
 Run actor 
 IRunActor  accepts  RunAgentDefinition ,  StartRun ,  ResumeRun ,  CancelRun ,  RecordAgentResponse , and  RecordAgentFailure . The run event stream records start, resume, completion, failure, cancellation, and individual agent outcomes.  GetRunState  returns a  RunSnapshot ;  GetRunStatus  returns the current status. A run ID is the durable correlation key across external execution and actor updates. 
 Install with  dotnet add package Troolio.Agents --version 10.0.8 , then register the actor assembly in the Orleans host and configure a compatible store. Build an application service around these contracts for scheduling, tool permissions, model calls, and idempotent delivery. Keep credentials and sensitive prompts out of public event payloads unless your retention and erasure design permits them. 
 Example: Create an agent and a run 
 These are the typed messages accepted by the definition and run actors. The host chooses actor IDs, persistence, authorization, and the external model execution service. 
 public static RegisterAgent DefineAgent(Metadata headers) =>
    new(headers, "Summarizer", "Assistant", "Summarize the input", "model-id");
 
 public static StartRun BeginRun(Metadata headers) =>
    new(headers, "summary-1", "Summarize this", [
        new RunAgentDefinition("agent-1", "Summarizer", "Assistant",
            "Summarize the input", "model-id")]);

title: SQL Server integration
description: SQL Server transactions, queues, routes, and recovery.
text:
SQL Server integration 
 Troolio.SqlServer  provides SQL Server implementations for atomic event transactions, selected-route evidence, projection queues, orchestration state, effect intents, and recovery. Install with  dotnet add package Troolio.SqlServer --version 10.0.8  when SQL Server is the persistence authority for a chosen route. On this page Choose the contract Operating a route Example: Freeze an event for SQL 
 Choose the contract 
 ISqlAtomicConnectionFactory  supplies database connections.  ISqlAtomicEventCodec  controls the persisted event format.  ISqlAtomicCommitPolicy  decides whether a participant may commit; discoverable policy variants provide additional review.  SqlAtomicTransactionEngine  implements commit and recovery paths, including contextual and no-op variants. Projection consumers apply committed handoffs through  ISqlAtomicProjectionApply . 
 The package includes disposable schema helpers for tests and reference deployments. They are not a substitute for an application-owned migration, locking, indexing, backup, and retention plan. A serving host must provide connection credentials, trusted route admission, actor authorization, erasure fences, and durable operation evidence. Check the selected route's required capabilities before directing commands to it. 
 Operating a route 
 Run migrations before traffic. Review stream families, ancillary writes, transaction isolation, deadlock handling, and exact event serialization. Monitor pending projection work, receipts, and route epoch changes. Retain completion evidence at least as long as commands can be retried. See  atomic commit ,  route authority , and  recovery . 
 Example: Freeze an event for SQL 
 An application codec turns a domain event into the exact bytes and type identifier that SQL will persist. Register a codec whose format can also read historical events. 
 public static SqlFrozenEvent FreezeSql(ISqlAtomicEventCodec codec, Metadata headers) =>
    codec.Freeze(new Incremented(headers));

title: KurrentDB integration
description: KurrentDB append and selected-route integration.
text:
KurrentDB integration 
 Troolio.KurrentDB  provides event-stream adapters for ordinary append and selected routes, projection queue support, host pinning, committed-effect handling, and recovery checks. Install with  dotnet add package Troolio.KurrentDB --version 10.0.8  when the application uses KurrentDB streams. On this page Ordinary append Selected route Operations Example: Find a projection queue shard 
 Ordinary append 
 KurrentOrdinaryAppendAdapter  is governed by  ITrustedKurrentOrdinaryAppendAuthority  and  IKurrentOrdinaryAppendPolicy . The host supplies a trusted client, credentials, stream naming, ownership checks, and a policy for concurrent writes and deletion. Do not infer atomic multi-stream guarantees from an ordinary append. 
 Selected route 
 KurrentSelectedActorStore  uses a selected actor policy and event codec. Route admission, host pinning, recovery, and projection work have separate authority contracts. Review their implementation and configure a serving cohort before promoting a route. The combined  KurrentDB + SQL Server  package supplies a broker journal and coordination pieces when SQL-backed evidence is needed. 
 Operations 
 Protect event credentials and stream ACLs, define maximum event sizes and retention, and watch append conflicts and projection lag. Preserve exact event bytes and operation IDs through retries. A KurrentDB append and an external effect are separate durability domains; use  effect intents  and provider idempotency for side effects. 
 Example: Find a projection queue shard 
 A committed operation ID maps to one of the package’s stable projection queue shards. Use a namespace owned by your application. 
 public static string KurrentQueue(Guid operationId) =>
    KurrentProjectionQueue.Stream("orders", KurrentProjectionQueue.Shard(operationId));

title: KurrentDB with SQL Server
description: SQL journals and broker coordination for KurrentDB.
text:
KurrentDB with SQL Server 
 Troolio.KurrentDB.SqlServer  coordinates selected KurrentDB routes with SQL Server journals, admission evidence, projection consumption, and pending effect records. Install with  dotnet add package Troolio.KurrentDB.SqlServer --version 10.0.8  alongside the matching KurrentDB and SQL Server adapters when this route is chosen. On this page Coordination model Review before deployment Example: Apply one discovered operation 
 Coordination model 
 A trusted write broker owns operation journal decisions and talks to the KurrentDB append authority.  SqlKurrentBrokerOperationJournal  records durable operation evidence.  TrustedKurrentAdmissionGate  uses process and cohort snapshots to decide whether a worker may serve the route.  SqlKurrentBrokerSuccessorTakeover  supports controlled successor admission after a prior broker exits.  KurrentSqlProjectionConsumer  applies projection records through an application supplied  IKurrentSqlProjectionApply . 
 KurrentDB and SQL Server do not share a distributed transaction here. A crash between systems is resolved using journals, idempotent retries, and recovery checks. The host must preserve broker identity, journal retention, SQL migrations, KurrentDB access, and a policy for uncertain outcomes. Do not erase pending evidence to force a successor to start. 
 Review before deployment 
 Verify that both provider versions are 10.0.8; configure secure credentials and trusted transport; test broker failure at each append/journal boundary; monitor pending journals and projection lag. Read  recovery  and  deployment checklist . 
 Example: Apply one discovered operation 
 After configuring a trusted verifier and SQL projection writer, call the consumer from a scheduled worker. It returns an operation ID when one ready batch was applied. 
 public static Task<Guid?> ApplyCombined(KurrentSqlProjectionConsumer consumer,
    CancellationToken cancellationToken) =>
    consumer.ApplyPendingOnceAsync(cancellationToken: cancellationToken);

title: Security and retention
description: Ingress trust, credentials, erasure, and evidence lifetime.
text:
Security and retention 
 Troolio supplies contracts for actor messages and persistence, while the application host owns the security boundary. Authenticate requests before routing, authorize each command and target actor, and pass current principal evidence to selected routes. Correlation metadata is useful for tracing but is not an authorization token. On this page Data and credentials Evidence lifetime Example: Verify a trusted command identity Attribution and the current caller 
 Data and credentials 
 Keep database, KurrentDB, broker, and external-provider credentials in a secret manager controlled by the host. Apply transport security and least privilege at every provider connection. Events may be retained for replay; design payloads so private data has an explicit minimization, encryption, retention, and erasure policy. Consider snapshots, projection copies, journals, and backups together when fulfilling deletion requirements. 
 Evidence lifetime 
 An operation receipt, route fence, effect intent, or broker journal may be required to recognize a retry. Retain that evidence for the maximum supported retry horizon, then expire it under a documented process. Erasure and deletion fences must be checked under the same authority as ordinary appends and selected commits. A retry cannot bypass a current deletion fence just because a matching historical receipt exists. 
 Review the third-party notices inside each NuGet package before redistribution. See  route authority ,  external effects , and  deployment checklist . 
 Example: Verify a trusted command identity 
 The server compares a claim to the current authenticated principal, actor path, command type, and canonical bytes. A mismatch fails before selected-route execution. 
 public static TrustedAtomicCommandIdentity VerifyIdentity(
    byte[] serverKey, TrustedAtomicCommandIdentityClaim claim,
    byte[] canonicalCommand) =>
    TrustedAtomicCommandIdentityAuthority.Verify(serverKey, claim,
        "user-42", "CounterActor/42", nameof(Increment), canonicalCommand);
 
 Attribution and the current caller 
 Message metadata  distinguishes acting users, owners, and recipients.  Read-model design  shows explicit access enforcement and filtered SQL reads. A correlation or user header is not proof of current permission.

title: Testing applications
description: Test actor logic, provider guarantees, and recovery.
text:
Testing applications 
 Test a Troolio application at the contract boundaries it actually deploys. A unit test can check event decisions and replay; it cannot prove store atomicity, route admission, or crash recovery. On this page Useful test layers Example: Assert the completion receipt Test whole application stories 
 Useful test layers 
 
 Actor logic:  issue commands, inspect emitted events, replay them, and verify queries. Cover duplicate creation, stale versions, and invalid transitions. 
 Store conformance:  reject a changed batch with the same operation ID, stale expected versions, stale route epochs, and deleted owners. Prove that ancillary streams, projection handoffs, and receipt commit together. 
 Subscriber and effect recovery:  crash between claim and completion, retry a provider with the same idempotency key, and verify a definitive terminal receipt. 
 Provider integration:  use real SQL Server or KurrentDB for locking, transactions, migration, credentials, and broker failover checks. 
 Package consumer:  restore the exact public package versions into an empty-cache .NET 10 project and compile a host with the adapters it actually uses. 
 
 Adapt these layers to your own actor and provider policies. See  first actor ,  atomic commit , and  recovery . 
 Example: Assert the completion receipt 
 Tests for a selected route should inspect the durable receipt as well as resulting stream versions and projection handoffs. 
 public static void CheckReceipt(AtomicEventTransactionReceipt receipt)
{
    if (!receipt.AncillaryWritesCommitted || !receipt.ProjectionHandoffsCommitted)
        throw new InvalidOperationException("Commit is incomplete.");
}
 
 Test whole application stories 
 Use the  workshop workflow  to exercise request, duplicate request, cancellation, replay, projection redelivery, and an authorized read. Verify that historical replay produces no notification or orchestration effects, that current ownership filters every query, and that a delayed add cannot resurrect a cancelled registration.

title: Upgrade and migration
description: Move a host to 10.0.6 with replay, schema, and route checks.
text:
Upgrade and migration 
 Troolio 10.0.8 is the first public five-package cohort: Core plus Agents, SQL Server, KurrentDB, and the combined KurrentDB/SQL adapter. Existing hosts on Core 10.0.5 should review package changes and provider requirements before upgrading. The new adapter IDs do not automatically activate routes or migrate data. On this page Prepare Roll out 
 Prepare 
 
 Inventory the current Troolio and Orleans versions, actor assemblies, stream formats, serializers, schemas, and hosted workers. Pin all chosen Troolio packages to 10.0.8. 
 Back up event streams, SQL journals, projections, and operation evidence. Record the current route epoch and deployment fingerprint if a selected path is already in use. 
 Build the application against the new packages and run actor replay tests with representative historical events. Check event type names and serialized bytes before any production rollout. 
 Apply application-owned database migrations and verify connection, lock, ownership, retention, and erasure policies. Do not use disposable test schemas as production migrations. 
 Test projection catch-up, retry identity, effect idempotency, and a worker crash near each provider boundary. 
 
 Roll out 
 Deploy compatible hosts and admit the reviewed serving cohort. For selected routes, promote the route epoch under its authoritative store and prevent older workers from writing. Watch append conflicts, projection backlog, effect intents, and broker journals. Keep rollback procedures tied to a verified state of streams and schema; event format changes may need a forward fix rather than a binary downgrade. 
 See  packages ,  deployment checklist , and  recovery .

title: Troubleshooting
description: Investigate conflicts, pending work, and uncertain outcomes.
text:
Troubleshooting 
 Start with the operation ID and the authoritative provider record. A client timeout alone does not establish whether the command committed. On this page Example: Check the authoritative head 
 
 
 
 Symptom 
 Check 
 
 
 
 
 Version conflict 
 Current stream head, expected version, and actor ownership. 
 
 
 Stale route 
 Route key, epoch, deployment fingerprint, silo admission, and promotion record. 
 
 
 Duplicate operation rejected 
 Canonical request identity and exact serialized event batch; a changed retry is invalid. 
 
 
 Projection lag 
 Persisted handoff or queue marker, consumer checkpoint, and application apply errors. 
 
 
 Pending external effect 
 Intent, provider availability, stable idempotency key, and terminal receipt. 
 
 
 Broker takeover blocked 
 SQL journal, KurrentDB stream evidence, trusted process roster, and predecessor state. 
 
 
 
 Do not retry with a new operation ID until the original outcome is known. Do not clear projection markers, intent rows, or broker journals to make a dashboard green. Preserve logs with correlation IDs and route epochs while investigating; avoid logging payload secrets. After determining the authoritative outcome, follow the provider's recovery procedure and test the same failure in a staging environment. 
 See  recovery ,  route authority , and the specific  integration guide . 
 Example: Check the authoritative head 
 When a client times out, read the current stream head before deciding whether to retry. For a selected route, also inspect the operation receipt and route fence. 
 public static Task<(IEvent? Event, ulong Version)> RecoveryHead(IStore store) =>
    store.ReadLastEvent("CounterActor-42");

title: Deployment checklist
description: Checks for a production host and providers.
text:
Deployment checklist 
 Use this checklist when promoting a Troolio host that serves persistent actor traffic. On this page Build and compatibility Authority and storage Work after commit 
 Build and compatibility 
 
 Pin all installed Troolio packages to 10.0.8 and use a compatible .NET 10 / Orleans 10 host. 
 Register the actor assemblies and the selected store/serializer explicitly. 
 Run package restore and integration tests against the same provider versions used in production. 
 
 Authority and storage 
 
 Authenticate and authorize ingress, actor targets, and selected routes. 
 Apply schema migrations and verify database transaction, locking, stream naming, and indexes. 
 Set the route epoch, reviewed deployment fingerprint, and serving silo/broker admission. 
 Define event retention, deletion fences, receipt lifetime, backups, and restoration drills. 
 
 Work after commit 
 
 Configure projection consumers, delivery workers, and retry scheduling. 
 Register external-effect providers with durable idempotency and pending-intent recovery. 
 Monitor queue lag, stale route rejects, append conflicts, operation receipts, and broker journals. 
 Test crashes before and after event append, receipt creation, projection claim, effect dispatch, and broker handoff. 
 
 An adapter package supplies code, not a production route by itself. The host owns the policies and operational controls. Start with  host setup , then  packages  and  recovery .

title: Projection catch-up and rebuilds
description: Recover missed deliveries and evolve views with bounded background work and durable progress.
text:
Projection catch-up and rebuilds 
 A projection can fall behind after a worker stops, SQL becomes unavailable, or a new view is introduced. Treat each case as explicit work with a source, destination, progress record, and failure policy. Restoring an actor's state does not repair all its read models automatically. On this page Distinguish the tasks Bound one work unit Keep serving and recovery separate Introduce a projection version Invalid data and access changes Retain useful progress 
 Distinguish the tasks 
 
 
 
 Task 
 Purpose 
 
 
 
 
 Delivery recovery 
 Retry committed handoff work that a consumer has not acknowledged. 
 
 
 Catch-up 
 Advance an existing projection from a known source cursor. 
 
 
 Rebuild 
 Populate a new version of a read model from verified history. 
 
 
 Data repair 
 Correct a specific invalid or missing view under an audited application policy. 
 
 
 
 The same pure mapper can support more than one task, but a rebuild should not run business orchestration or external notification providers just because it reads historical events. 
 Bound one work unit 
 The example worker reads one page of verified rows, applies each idempotently, and advances its partition cursor. The application interfaces own verified source reads and durable compare-and-swap progress. 
 public static class ProjectionRepair
{
    public static async Task ProcessPageAsync(string partition, IRepairFeed feed,
        IRegistrationCardWriter writer, IRepairProgress progress, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
    {
        string? cursor = await progress.LoadAsync(partition, cancellationToken);
        RepairPage page = await feed.ReadAsync(partition, cursor, 100, cancellationToken);
        if (page.Items.Count > 100) throw new InvalidDataException("Repair page exceeded its bound.");
        foreach (RepairItem item in page.Items)
            await writer.ApplyAsync(item.Card, item.Source, cancellationToken);
        // A crash before this point repeats the page; the writer deduplicates source records.
        if (!await progress.AdvanceAsync(partition, cursor, page.NextCursor, cancellationToken))
            throw new InvalidOperationException("Another worker advanced this repair partition.");
    }
}
 
 A crash before cursor advancement repeats the page. The projection writer's retained source identities make that repetition safe. The compare-and-swap failure tells the worker that another process advanced the partition; it cannot silently overwrite that progress. 
 This helper is one bounded work unit. A host scheduler supplies worker lifecycle, admission, leases where needed, time limits, backoff, and metrics. The interface implementations must check that the source and cursor belong to the expected partition and that a returned page cannot exceed its bound. 
 Keep serving and recovery separate 
 Avoid startup routines that scan every registration to reconstruct global read state. Their cost grows with application history, and one bad stream can delay global availability. 
 Startup can check required infrastructure and establish consumers. Repair workers can advance affected partitions in the background. The relevant endpoint should know whether its view is ready, catching up, unavailable, or quarantined. Do not represent missing projection data as a confidently empty catalogue. 
 Introduce a projection version 
 For a substantial change, create a new consumer identity and target schema, such as a second registration-card version. Populate it from verified source history, catch up with live traffic, compare the query behavior, then promote the readers. Keep a rollback or forward-fix plan based on compatible schemas and retained source data. 
 One useful cutover records a source boundary, backfills through that boundary, applies later live work, and checks the remaining lag before switching readers. The mechanism must fit your provider: a multi-stream application may need per-stream positions or committed operation groups rather than one global integer. 
 Do not clear an existing consumer's inbox and point the same identity at a new schema without deciding what delayed deliveries and old acknowledgements mean. 
 Invalid data and access changes 
 Transient connection failures can be retried. A source that cannot be decoded into the expected event schema needs an identifiable quarantine outcome and repair decision. Continue independent partitions where the provider permits it. 
 Current deletion and access fences also apply to rebuilt views. Historical ownership alone does not grant a restored view permission to expose deleted or inaccessible data. Coordinate projection repair with the application's retention and erasure policy. 
 Retain useful progress 
 Track the projection version, source partition, cursor, attempt count, last successful advance, and failure category. Keep private domain payloads out of routine progress logs. Monitor the oldest pending work as well as counts; a small permanently stuck partition can be more serious than a briefly large queue. 
 Continue with  replay and live events ,  projection design , and  observability .

Packages and compatibility 
 Troolio targets .NET 10 and Microsoft Orleans 10. The framework and optional samples-repository extensions have separate version lines. On this page Framework packages Optional extensions Choose a runnable example Message serialization

 Keep these framework packages together at  10.0.8  when installing more than one:

dotnet add package Troolio.Stores.EventStore --version 10.0.2
 
 The EventStore and Marten extensions implement ordinary actor storage. They are not substitutes for the framework's selected atomic-route contracts. EF and Redis are read-side integrations; selecting either does not establish a durable event-to-projection outbox or a global transaction. Configure those contracts explicitly when the application requires them.

title: Glossary
description: Terms used across Troolio guides.
text:
Glossary 
 
 
 
 Term 
 Meaning 
 
 
 
 
 Actor path 
 Stable identity of one actor, used in commands, ownership checks, and transaction participants. 
 
 
 Stream 
 Ordered event history for one stream name and version sequence. 
 
 
 Event 
 Immutable fact produced by a command and later replayed to reconstruct state. 
 
 
 Projection 
 Consumer that turns committed events into a read-oriented view. 
 
 
 Handoff 
 Durable marker or queue record connecting committed events to a projection consumer. 
 
 
 Operation ID 
 Stable identifier for one command attempt and its retries. 
 
 
 Request identity 
 Canonical SHA-256 digest of the original command identity and payload. 
 
 
 Participant 
 Actor/stream, expected version, and events included in one closed atomic batch. 
 
 
 Route fence 
 Route key, epoch, and deployment fingerprint checked during selected commit. 
 
 
 Completion receipt 
 Durable evidence of what committed for an operation. 
 
 
 Event-only closure 
 Bounded planning of causal subscriber events before a selected commit. 
 
 
 External-effect intent 
 Durable record of a side effect to perform after event commit with a stable idempotency key. 
 
 
 Broker journal 
 Durable evidence coordinating a KurrentDB write broker with SQL state. 
 
 
 
 Follow  selected command route  for the full request path or  recovery  for retry semantics. On this page Message identity terms 
 Message identity terms 
 
 
 
 Term 
 Meaning 
 
 
 
 
 Correlation ID 
 Groups a chosen user interaction or workflow for investigation. 
 
 
 Causation ID 
 Links a message to the message that directly caused it. 
 
 
 Message ID 
 Identifies a message/runtime dispatch within the correlation story. 
 
 
 User ID 
 Attributed user, bound to authenticated context at ingress. 
 
 
 Device ID 
 Originating device/session context under application policy. 
 
 
 Transaction ID 
 Troolio transaction context supplied by the command protocol. 
 
 
 Source actor ID 
 EventEnvelope.Id , the source actor key shared by its delivered events. 
 
 
 Projection inbox 
 Retained source-processing identity committed with the view update. 
 
 
 Refresh hint 
 Reference indicating that a client should make another authorized read. 
 
 
 Tombstone 
 Retained lifecycle evidence preventing delayed work from recreating a removed entry. 
 
 
 
 Read  message metadata  and  correlation and causation  for examples, then  idempotency and ordering  for retry identity.

title: Build the ToDo API
description: Follow HTTP commands, pure replay and durable SQLite read models.
text:
ToDo: actors, events and durable SQL reads 
 A beginner-friendly .NET 10 application using actual Troolio actors. Run the API, open its browser page, create a todo and complete it. Each todo owns an event stream. Live committed events update a SQLite read model through the EF projection extension. Queries read SQLite directly. On this page Run without Docker HTTP walkthrough Understand the code Identity and metadata Change event storage Explore the complete source 
 
 
 
 Package 
 Used for 
 
 
 
 
 Troolio.Core 
 Typed event-sourced actors, metadata, hosting and development event stores 
 
 
 Troolio.Projection.EntityFramework 
 Awaited live relational projection operations 
 
 
 Troolio.Stores.EventStore 
 Optional gRPC event persistence with KurrentDB 
 
 
 Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Sqlite 
 Durable local read-model database 
 
 
 Microsoft.Orleans.Sdk 
 Build-time message serialization and actor code generation 
 
 
 
 Run without Docker 
 Install the .NET 10 SDK, then from the repository root: 
 dotnet run --project Sample/ToDo.EventStoreEfApi --urls http://localhost:5080
 
 Open  http://localhost:5080 .  wwwroot/index.html  is the browser client. The default  FileSystem  event store writes to  todo-events  in the process working directory; SQLite writes  todo-readmodels.db . Keep both directories/files to preserve state across restarts. These development defaults use one local Orleans silo, memory stream delivery and memory reminders. They are not a clustered production deployment. 
 
 Existing prototype data 
 This example replaces the old handwritten event bus. Its event shapes and SQLite owner column differ from the prototype. Preserve any useful prototype data separately and start this learning sample with a fresh event folder and read-model database.  EnsureCreated  creates a new demonstration schema; it does not migrate an existing database. A real application uses reviewed EF migrations and explicit event-schema evolution. 
 HTTP walkthrough 
 Create a todo. Supplying a stable ID makes retries safe; omitting it generates a new ID for each request. 
 curl http://localhost:5080/todos \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'X-Correlation-Id: aaaaaaaa-aaaa-aaaa-aaaa-aaaaaaaaaaaa' \
  -d '{"id":"22222222-2222-2222-2222-222222222222","title":"Learn event sourcing"}'

curl http://localhost:5080/todos/22222222-2222-2222-2222-222222222222
curl -X POST http://localhost:5080/todos/22222222-2222-2222-2222-222222222222/complete
curl http://localhost:5080/todos
 
 
 
 
 Request 
 Result 
 
 
 
 
 Create valid todo 
 201 Created ; same owner, ID and title retry emits no new event 
 
 
 Create same ID with another title 
 409 Conflict 
 
 
 Empty/too long title or empty supplied ID 
 400 Bad Request 
 
 
 Complete existing owned todo 
 202 Accepted ; repeated completion emits no new event 
 
 
 Complete missing todo 
 404 Not Found 
 
 
 Complete another owner's todo 
 403 Forbidden 
 
 
 Get missing/unowned todo 
 404 Not Found 
 
 
 Get list 
 Caller-filtered SQL page;  skip=0 ,  take=50 , maximum 100 
 
 
 GET /health 
 Process readiness after silo and database startup 
 
 
 
 The API awaits the actor command and event append. The memory stream delivers live projections asynchronously; the EF consumer awaits each SQLite write and propagates a failed write to its delivery pipeline. Queries can briefly return the previous read model. The browser refreshes until the change appears. This ordinary store/projection combination does not provide an atomic event-plus-read-model transaction or durable projection outbox. A production design needs explicit consumer recovery and projection repair; retain the read database on restart, and never silently rebuild it by scanning every stream at startup. 
 Understand the code 
 1. Commands express intent 
 TodoDomain.cs  defines messages and their owning actor. Orleans serializer member IDs are explicit and stable; retain existing IDs when messages evolve. 
 [GenerateSerializer]
public sealed record CreateTodoCommand(Metadata Headers,
    [property: Id(0)] Guid TodoId,
    [property: Id(1)] string Title) : Command<ITodoActor>(Headers);
 
 The API validates input before dispatch. The actor repeats domain validation because future callers may bypass HTTP.  TodoId  is the actor's key and the business retry key. A conflicting reuse of the key fails. 
 if (State.TodoId != Guid.Empty)
{
    if (State.OwnerId != command.Headers.UserId)
        throw new UnauthorizedAccessException();
    if (State.Title != command.Title)
        throw new InvalidOperationException("This ID already has a different title.");
    return []; // The same business operation already succeeded.
}
 
 2. Events describe what happened 
 The actor returns an event; Troolio appends it and applies it to actor state. Domain timestamps are captured when handling the command, then persisted in the event. 
 return [new TodoCreated(command.Headers, command.TodoId,
    command.Headers.UserId, command.Title, DateTimeOffset.UtcNow)];
 
 3. State replay is pure 
 TodoState.Apply  restores state from recorded facts. Activation reads only the owning actor's stream. These reducers never write SQL, send a notification or execute another command. 
 public TodoState Apply(TodoCreated e) =>
    new(e.TodoId, e.OwnerId, e.Title, false, e.CreatedAt, null);

public TodoState Apply(TodoCompleted e) =>
    this with { IsCompleted = true, CompletedAt = e.CompletedAt };

public void On(TodoCreated e) => State = State.Apply(e);
public void On(TodoCompleted e) => State = State.Apply(e);
 
 4. A live projection creates the query view 
 TodoProjection.cs  subscribes to live  TodoActor  events. Its mappings create/update relational entities; the extension awaits persistence and propagates failures. 
 [ProjectionStreamSubscription(nameof(TodoActor))]
public sealed class TodoEfProjection
    : EntityFrameworkBatchedProjection<TodoReadModel, TodoReadModelDbContext>,
      ITodoEfProjection
{
    public Task On(EventEnvelope<TodoCreated> e) => Create(e);
    public Task On(EventEnvelope<TodoCompleted> e) => Update(e);
    // SetupMappings defines the entity fields; see the complete source file.
}
 
 EventEnvelope.Id  is the source actor key.  Stream  plus  Version  locates the event in its source stream; it is not the same thing as a request or event message ID. The EF adapter's existing-key create handling is a basic duplicate safeguard, not a durable inbox for every possible operation. 
 5. Read SQL without waking every actor 
 List and detail endpoints query the durable model with the current server identity. A list never loads all todo streams.  GET /todos?skip=0&take=50  reads a bounded SQL page; the maximum page size is 100. The SQLite mapping stores creation timestamps as UTC ticks so ordering stays inside the database. 
 var todos = await db.Todos.AsNoTracking()
    .Where(x => x.OwnerId == identity.UserId)
    .OrderByDescending(x => x.CreatedAt).ThenBy(x => x.Id)
    .Skip(skip).Take(take).ToListAsync();
 
 Identity and metadata 
 The sample has one server-configured demonstration identity,  Todo:DemoUserId . Everyone using the local API acts as that user. It deliberately accepts no client  X-User-Id  authority. Replace  DemoIdentity  with a verified authenticated principal before exposing this application beyond local learning. 
 return new Metadata(correlationId, identity.UserId, Guid.Empty);
 
 
 
 
 Field 
 Meaning in this sample 
 
 
 
 
 CorrelationId 
 Diagnostic ID shared by a request flow; valid  X-Correlation-Id  is echoed in the response 
 
 
 UserId 
 Actor owner identity supplied by trusted server configuration 
 
 
 DeviceId 
 Guid.Empty ; no verified device identity is available 
 
 
 MessageId 
 Troolio assigns runtime message identities; do not use it as the todo retry key 
 
 
 CausationId 
 Troolio stamps emitted events with the handled command's message ID 
 
 
 TransactionId 
 Framework metadata for the ordinary command flow; it does not imply an atomic SQLite transaction with the event store 
 
 
 
 Change event storage 
 TodoRuntime.cs  builds exactly one  TroolioServer  host and uses its actor system for API commands. The web host owns startup and shutdown.  FileSystem  is the default;  InMemory  is available only for temporary demonstrations and loses all events on restart. 
 For a local KurrentDB/EventStore-compatible gRPC endpoint, set: 
 Todo__EventStore=EventStore \
EventStore__ConnectionString='esdb://localhost:2113?tls=false' \
dotnet run --project Sample/ToDo.EventStoreEfApi --urls http://localhost:5080
 
 The retained  Troolio.Stores.EventStore  package now uses gRPC rather than legacy TCP. Production endpoints require appropriate TLS and credentials, provided through your host configuration/secret manager. 
 services.AddSingleton(new KurrentDBClient(
    KurrentDBClientSettings.Create(connectionString)));
// TodoRuntime selects TroolioServer<ESStore, JsonEventSerializer>(...).
 
 Port defaults are  19220  (silo) and  19221  (gateway). Change  Todo:SiloPort  and  Todo:GatewayPort  to run another local instance. Each independent demonstration instance also needs its own event folder and SQLite database. Sharing FileSystemStore across processes is unsupported. 
 Explore the complete source 
 Open the ToDo application on GitHub . The source includes the domain, hosting setup, SQLite mapping, browser client and HTTP contract. 
 The sample consumes Troolio.Core 10.0.8, Troolio.Projection.EntityFramework 10.0.2 and Troolio.Stores.EventStore 10.0.2. See  EF projections  and  ordinary gRPC event storage  to use the extensions in your own application.

title: Ordinary gRPC event storage
description: Use the EventStore extension with current KurrentDB transport.
text:
Ordinary gRPC event storage 
 Supported gRPC persistence for ordinary Troolio actors using KurrentDB. The historical package ID remains available; the deprecated TCP transport has been replaced. Requires .NET 10 and Troolio.Core 10.0.8. On this page Register the client and ordinary store Append with concurrency control Link streams and snapshots Migration and delivery limits Run an HTTP application Choose the correct Kurrent integration 
 dotnet add package Troolio.Stores.EventStore --version 10.0.2
 
 Register the client and ordinary store 
 The host owns a reusable client. Credentials and TLS belong in application configuration, not source code. 
 services.AddSingleton(_ => new KurrentDBClient(
    KurrentDBClientSettings.Create(configuration.GetConnectionString("EventStore")!)));
services.AddSingleton<ESStore>();
 
 Use  TroolioServer<ESStore>  when building the Troolio host. Its serialization and logging services supply the remaining constructor arguments: 
 IHost host = Host.CreateDefaultBuilder().TroolioServer<ESStore>(
    "Tasks", new[] { typeof(TaskActor).Assembly }, services =>
    {
        services.AddSingleton(_ => new KurrentDBClient(
            KurrentDBClientSettings.Create(connectionString)));
    });
await host.StartAsync();
 
 Configure the host's Orleans membership/storage profile separately. The convenience  Startup.RunWithDefaults  wrapper reads  ConnectionStrings:EventStore  from appsettings and environment variables.  ES.CreateClient(connectionString)  creates a client; it does not use a global static connection. 
 A local disposable insecure node can use  esdb://localhost:2113?tls=false . Production should use TLS and credentials, for example  esdb://user:password@server:2113?tls=true , supplied securely through configuration. 
 Append with concurrency control 
 A stream head of 0 means no events. Troolio event versions start at 1; KurrentDB revisions start at 0. The adapter performs that translation and throws Troolio's  WrongExpectedVersionException  on a conflicting append. 
 IEvent[] events = { new TaskRenamed(taskId, "New title", headers) };
ulong appended = await store.Append(streamName, expectedVersion, events);
IEvent[] tail = await store.ReadStreamFromEvent(streamName, expectedVersion + 1);
(IEvent? last, ulong head) = await store.ReadLastEvent(streamName);
 
 Events retain serialized metadata including correlation, causation, user, device and transaction IDs. An event's message ID supplies its storage identity when present. Empty appends write nothing. Unknown event types or invalid payloads fail explicitly; they are not silently dropped from actor replay. 
 Link streams and snapshots 
 Linked read models refer to source stream/version pairs. The adapter writes the KurrentDB link representation and resolves it on reads. 
 await store.Append(readModelStream, linkHead,
    new IEvent[] { new LinkEvent(Guid.NewGuid(), sourceVersion, sourceStream) });
IEvent? sourceEvent = await store.ReadStreamEvent(readModelStream, linkHead + 1);
 
 The link stream retains its own version even when the resolved source event has a different source version. Keep source events available for the lifetime of linked read models. Typed actor snapshot events use the same serializer and ordinary persistence API. 
 Migration and delivery limits 
 Replace old TCP host/port settings and global  ES.Connection  registration with the injected gRPC client. KurrentDB versions without TCP support can now be used. This package preserves ordinary event CLR type names and serialized payloads; retain event types/aliases and validate historical data before renaming application types. 
 This adapter implements ordinary  IStore .  Troolio.KurrentDB  provides separate policy/authority-driven selected transaction capabilities; it is not a drop-in ordinary store replacement. Domain append here does not automatically provide durable projection dispatch, a SQL inbox or atomic cross-actor operations.
